### Setup project and run tests

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/packages/bun-plugin-yaml/README.md

Install dependencies and execute the test suite when contributing to the plugin.

```bash
$ bun install # project setup
$ bun test # run tests
```

--------------------------------

### Install a package globally with bun install --global

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx

Use the -g or --global flag to install a command-line tool globally. This example installs cowsay and then runs it.

```bash
bun install --global cowsay # or `bun install -g cowsay`
cowsay "Bun!"
```

--------------------------------

### Setup logic in package.json bun-create section

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/templating/create.mdx

Specify pre- and post-install setup scripts in the "bun-create" section of a local template's package.json. preinstall and postinstall accept a string or an array of strings; arrays run in order. Commands run through the shell in the destination folder, and bun create stops with a non-zero code if a command or bun install fails.

```json
{
  "name": "@bun-examples/simplereact",
  "version": "0.0.1",
  "main": "index.js",
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^17.0.2",
    "react-dom": "^17.0.2"
  },
  "bun-create": {
    "preinstall": "echo 'Installing...'", // a single command
    "postinstall": ["echo 'Done!'"], // an array of commands
    "start": "bun run echo 'Hello world!'"
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Valid shortened import paths example setup

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/import/no-useless-path-segments.mdx

Demonstrates valid, simplified relative import paths in src/pages/home.js that are not reported.

```js
export function formatDate() {}
```

```js
export function Header() {}
```

```js
import { formatDate } from "../format.js";
import { Header } from "./header.js";
```

--------------------------------

### Install all project dependencies

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx

Run `bun install` without arguments to install all dependencies listed in `package.json`. This installs `dependencies`, `devDependencies`, and `optionalDependencies`, and also installs `peerDependencies` by default. It runs `{pre|post}install` and `{pre|post}prepare` scripts, and writes a `bun.lock` lockfile.

```bash
bun install
```

--------------------------------

### Install dependencies with bun install

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/src/runtime/cli/init/README.default.md

Run this command to install the project's dependencies.

```bash
bun install
```

### Example output when using .prettierrc with plugins

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/format/migrate-from-prettier.mdx

Shows how Bun reports which files are formatted natively and which are passed to your installed Prettier when a .prettierrc config includes plugins.

```txt
Using .prettierrc (Prettier config)

    3 files are formatted natively
    1 file goes to your installed Prettier: 1 *.astro

Built-in plugins: @ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports
Plugins that use your installed Prettier: prettier-plugin-astro

Still needed:   @ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports, prettier, prettier-plugin-astro (some files go to them)
```

--------------------------------

### Valid single and nested hooks example

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/bun-test/no-duplicate-hooks.mdx

Demonstrates valid hook usage by combining setup actions into a single `beforeEach` per block or isolating them into nested `describe` blocks.

```ts
import { beforeEach, describe, test } from "bun:test";

describe("cart", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cart.clear();
    cart.add("apple");
  });

  test("has one item", () => {});

  describe("after checkout", () => {
    beforeEach(() => {
      cart.checkout();
    });

    test("is empty", () => {});
  });
});

```

--------------------------------

### Install Bun in GitHub Actions with setup-bun

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/install/cicd.mdx

Use the official oven-sh/setup-bun action in a GitHub Actions runner step to install Bun and execute commands like bun install.

```yaml
name: my-workflow
jobs:
  my-job:
    name: my-job
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # ...
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2 # [!code ++]

      # run any `bun` or `bunx` command
      - run: bun install # [!code ++]
```

These examples are not reported because they use valid label reference syntax: `[guide][]`, `[guide]`, and `[this][guide]`.

Read the [guide][], the [guide], or [this][guide].

[guide]: https://example.com/guide
```

--------------------------------

### Set up toolchains and run homepage benchmarks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/bench/site/README.md

Sets up required toolchains and repositories, then executes the benchmark suite using a specified Bun binary under test. Supports running full suites, specific sub-benchmarks, or quick smoke tests via environment variables.

```sh
bench/site/setup-toolchains.sh                      # node, deno, pnpm/yarn/npm, bun release + canary -> $SITEBENCH_HOME/toolchains
bench/site/setup-repos.sh                           # rolldown/benchmarks clone + deps of bench/express, bench/websocket-server, bench/postgres
BUN=/abs/path/to/bun bench/site/run-all.sh          # everything: bundler http ws postgres install (~30 min with RUNS=3)
BUN=/abs/path/to/bun bench/site/run-all.sh http ws  # a subset
RUNS=1 BUN=... bench/site/run-all.sh                # quick smoke run
```

### Disallowed hook usage in test setup

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/vitest/no-hooks.mdx

An example of test setup using `beforeEach` that triggers a lint rule report.

```ts
import { beforeEach, expect, test } from "vitest";

let cart;

beforeEach(() => {
  cart = createCart();
});

test("starts empty", () => {
  expect(cart.items).toEqual([]);
});
```

--------------------------------

### Valid test setup inside hooks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/bun-test/require-hook.mdx

Example of compliant test structure with setup logic placed inside `beforeAll` and `beforeEach` hooks.

```ts
import { beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, mock, setDefaultTimeout, test } from "bun:test";

setDefaultTimeout(10_000);
mock.module("./mailer", () => ({ send: mock() }));

const names = ["ada", "grace"];
let db;

beforeAll(() => {
  db = connect();
  db.seed(names);
});

describe("users", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    clearCache();
  });

  test("finds a user", () => {
    expect(db.find("ada")).toBeDefined();
  });
});
```

### Start an HTTP server with Bun.serve

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/bun-apis.mdx

Starts an HTTP server using `Bun.serve` with standard `Request` and `Response` objects in server.ts.

```ts
Bun.serve({
  fetch(req: Request) {
    return new Response("Success!");
  },
});
```

const mode = flags | Mode.Write;

```

### Explicit setup within test without hooks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/vitest/no-hooks.mdx

An example of self-contained test setup that avoids shared hook state and passes the lint rule.

```ts
import { expect, test } from "vitest";

test("starts empty", () => {
  const cart = createCart();
  expect(cart.items).toEqual([]);
});
```

### Valid comments example

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/eslint/capitalized-comments.mdx

Demonstrates allowed comments: starting with an uppercase letter, starting with a number, containing a URL, or matching tool directives like eslint-disable.

```js
// Retry once, then give up
await send(message);

// 3 attempts at most
// https://example.com/retries explains why
/* eslint-disable-next-line no-console */
console.log("sent");
```

### Install without devDependencies using bun install --production

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx

Installs in production mode, omitting devDependencies. --production implies --frozen-lockfile and only controls what gets installed; devDependencies already in node_modules remain, so use bun prune --production to remove them.

```bash
bun install --production
```

--------------------------------

### Add start script to package.json

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/quickstart.mdx

Configure a start script in package.json to run the TypeScript entrypoint with Bun.

```json
{
  "name": "my-app",
  "module": "index.ts",
  "type": "module",
  "private": true,
  "scripts": { // [!code ++]
    "start": "bun run index.ts" // [!code ++]
  }, // [!code ++]
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/bun": "latest"
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "typescript": "^7"
  }
}
```

```bash

bun install react@19.1.1 # specific version
bun install react@latest # specific tag
```

### Get nanoseconds since process start with Bun.nanoseconds()

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/utils.mdx

Returns the number of nanoseconds since the current bun process started, as a number. Useful for high-precision timing and benchmarking.

```ts
Bun.nanoseconds();
// => 7288958
```

### Global test setup with beforeAll and afterAll hooks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/test/configuration.mdx

Define database setup and teardown handlers using `bun:test` hooks in a preload script.

```typescript
// Global test setup
import { beforeAll, afterAll } from "bun:test";

beforeAll(() => {
  // Set up test database
  setupTestDatabase();
});

afterAll(() => {
  // Clean up
  cleanupTestDatabase();
});
```

--------------------------------

### Configure global installation behavior in ~/.bunfig.toml

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/add.mdx

Set globalDir and globalBinDir in the global .bunfig.toml ($HOME/.bunfig.toml or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/.bunfig.toml). Bun ignores these keys in a project's bunfig.toml.

```toml
[install]
# where `bun add --global` installs packages
globalDir = "~/.bun/install/global"

# where globally-installed package bins are linked
globalBinDir = "~/.bun/bin"
```

### Reported regular expression starting with `=`

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/eslint/no-div-regex.mdx

Example of regular expression syntax reported by `no-div-regex` due to ambiguity with `/=`.

```js
const value = line.replace(/=\s*/, "");
```

--------------------------------

### bunx command syntax

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/snippets/cli/bunx.mdx

General invocation form for bunx. Executes an npm package executable (CLI); if the package isn't installed in node_modules, Bun installs it into a global shared cache.

```bash
bunx [flags] <package>[@version] [flags and arguments for the package]
```

--------------------------------

### Reported usage of beforeEach hook

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/jest/no-hooks.mdx

Example of test setup using `beforeEach` that triggers the `jest/no-hooks` lint rule violation.

```ts
import { beforeEach, expect, test } from "@jest/globals";

let cart;

beforeEach(() => {
  cart = createCart();
});

test("starts empty", () => {
  expect(cart.items).toEqual([]);
});
```

Initialize a new SvelteKit project using the Svelte CLI via `bunx sv create` and select Bun as the package manager during prompt setup.

```txt
┌  Welcome to the Svelte CLI! (v0.5.7)
│
◇  Which template would you like?
│  SvelteKit demo

│

│  bun
│
◇  Successfully installed dependencies
│
◇  Project next steps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                          │
│  1: cd my-app                                                            │
│  2: git init && git add -A && git commit -m "Initial commit" (optional)  │
│  3: bun run dev -- --open                                                │
│                                                                          │
│  To close the dev server, hit Ctrl-C                                     │
│                                                                          │
│  Stuck? Visit us at https://svelte.dev/chat                              │
│                                                                          │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
│
└  You're all set!
```

### Valid comments example

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/eslint/no-warning-comments.mdx

Shows valid comments that do not trigger the rule because warning terms are not matching whole words at the start.

```js
// An empty list gives 0.
function total(items) {
  // Todos are counted like any other item.
  return items.length * 1.1;
}
```

### Avoid reporting by not exporting unimported functions

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/import/no-unused-modules.mdx

Example setup where `formatTime` in `shop/format.js` is not exported, avoiding lint warnings for unused exports.

```json
{
  "root": true,
  "plugins": ["import"],
  "parserOptions": { "ecmaVersion": "latest", "sourceType": "module" },
  "rules": { "import/no-unused-modules": ["error", { "unusedExports": true }] }
}
```

```js
import { formatDate } from "./format.js";

console.log(formatDate(new Date()));
```

```js
export function formatDate(date) {}
function formatTime(date) {}
```

### Start a simple HTTP server with Bun.serve

Starts an HTTP server listening on port 3000 that responds to every request with status 200 and "Welcome to Bun!".

```typescript
const server = Bun.serve({
  port: 3000,
  fetch(request) {
    return new Response("Welcome to Bun!");
  },
});

console.log(`Listening on ${server.url}`);
```

### Restricted modifier example (reported)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/bun-test/no-restricted-matchers.mdx

Demonstrates that restricting a modifier such as `{ resolves = "" }` causes all chains starting with `resolves` to be reported.

```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

test("loads the user", async () => {
  await expect(loadUser(1)).resolves.toEqual({ id: 1 });
  await expect(loadUser(2)).resolves.not.toBeNull();
});
```

--------------------------------

### Implement a custom Bun plugin

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/bundler/fullstack.mdx

Create a plugin that exports a BunPlugin object with a name and setup function. The example loads .custom files as JavaScript modules.

```typescript
import type { BunPlugin } from "bun";

const myPlugin: BunPlugin = {
  name: "my-custom-plugin",
  setup(build) {
    // Plugin implementation
    build.onLoad({ filter: /\.custom$/ }, async args => {
      const text = await Bun.file(args.path).text();
      return {
        contents: `export default ${JSON.stringify(text)};`,
        loader: "js",
      };
    });
  },
};

export default myPlugin;
```

### Autolink URLs with paths

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/js/bun/md/spec-permissive-autolinks.txt

Matches optional URL paths starting with '/' and delimited by slashes. Non-alphanumerical characters (., -, _) in path components must be bounded by alphanumerical characters.

```example
https://example.com/images/branding/logo_272x92.png

<p><a href="https://example.com/images/branding/logo_272x92.png">https://example.com/images/branding/logo_272x92.png</a></p>
.
--fpermissive-url-autolinks
```

### Serve frontend with Bun.serve and HTML imports

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/src/runtime/cli/init/rule.md

Demonstrates setting up a full-stack server using Bun.serve with route handlers, WebSockets, HTML imports, and React/CSS bundling. Run index.ts using bun --hot for hot reloading.

```ts
import index from "./index.html"

Bun.serve({
  routes: {
    "/": index,
    "/api/users/:id": {
      GET: (req) => {
        return new Response(JSON.stringify({ id: req.params.id }));
      },
    },
  },
  // optional websocket support
  websocket: {
    open: (ws) => {
      ws.send("Hello, world!");
    },
    message: (ws, message) => {
      ws.send(message);
    },
    close: (ws) => {
      // handle close
    }
  },
  development: {
    hmr: true,
    console: true,
  }
})
```

```html
<html>
  <body>
    <h1>Hello, world!</h1>
    <script type="module" src="./frontend.tsx"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

```tsx
import React from "react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";

// import .css files directly and it works
import './index.css';

const root = createRoot(document.body);

export default function Frontend() {
  return <h1>Hello, world!</h1>;
}

root.render(<Frontend />);
```

```sh
bun --hot ./index.ts
```

### Configure and start Bun app with pm2.config.cjs

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/pm2.mdx

Defines a PM2 configuration file pointing to the Bun interpreter and starts the daemonized process.

```javascript
module.exports = {
  name: "app", // Name of your application
  script: "index.ts", // Entry point of your application
  interpreter: "bun", // Bun interpreter
  env: {
    PATH: `${process.env.HOME}/.bun/bin:${process.env.PATH}`, // Add "~/.bun/bin/bun" to PATH
  },
};
```

```bash
pm2 start pm2.config.cjs
```

### Incorrect test blocks without padding (Reported)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/vitest/padding-around-test-blocks.mdx

Shows an example where test calls directly follow setup code and each other without separating blank lines, causing a lint violation.

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";

describe("cart", () => {
  const cart = createCart();
  test("starts empty", () => {
    expect(cart.items).toEqual([]);
  });
  test.skip("adds an item", () => {
    expect(cart.add("apple").items).toEqual(["apple"]);
  });
});
```

--------------------------------

### Define a cc rule and build edge in build.ninja

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/scripts/build/CLAUDE.md

Example from the generated build/<profile>/build.ninja showing a `cc` rule (defined via n.rule("cc", {...}) in compile.ts) and a build edge emitted by cc(n, cfg, src, opts) per source. The `|` starts implicit inputs and `||` starts order-only inputs.

```ninja
rule cc
  command = clang $cflags -MMD -MT $out -MF $out.d -c $in -o $out
  depfile = $out.d
  deps = gcc

build obj/src/foo.c.o: cc ../../src/foo.c | deps/zstd/libzstd.a || codegen/generated.h
  cflags = -O2 -I...
```

### Set scanner credentials via environment variables

### Invalid test code violating require-hook

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/bun-test/require-hook.mdx

Example of invalid test setup where initialized `let` variables and standalone function calls are placed outside hooks at the top level or directly in a `describe` block.

let db = connect();
db.seed(["ada", "grace"]);

  clearCache();

  test("finds a user", () => {
    expect(db.find("ada")).toBeDefined();
  });
});

### builder.onStart(callback)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/bundler/esbuild.mdx

Registers a callback that is called when the bundle starts. This hook is useful for initialization tasks before the bundling process begins.

```APIDOC
## builder.onStart(callback)

### Description
Registers a callback that is called when the bundle starts. This hook is useful for initialization tasks before the bundling process begins.

### Method
builder.onStart(callback: () => void): void

### Parameters
- **callback** (function) - Required - A function to be called when the bundle starts.

### Example
```ts
builder.onStart(() => {
  console.log('Bundle started');
});
```
```

### Report child process resource usage with resourceUsage()

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/child-process.mdx

After the spawned process exits, call resourceUsage() to get maxRSS and CPU time. The example spawns bun --version and logs memory and CPU usage.

```typescript
const proc = Bun.spawn(["bun", "--version"]);
await proc.exited;

const usage = proc.resourceUsage();
console.log(`Max memory used: ${usage.maxRSS} bytes`);
console.log(`CPU time (user): ${usage.cpuTime.user} µs`);
console.log(`CPU time (system): ${usage.cpuTime.system} µs`);
```

### package.json with a metadependency

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/overrides.mdx

Example package.json where foo depends on bar, making bar a metadependency. By default, Bun installs the latest version of all dependencies and metadependencies according to the ranges specified in each package's package.json.

```json
{
  "name": "my-app",
  "dependencies": {
    "foo": "^2.0.0"
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Retrieve rows as raw Buffers with sql.raw()

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/sql.mdx

Use .raw() to get rows as arrays of Buffer objects (Uint8Array on SQLite). Call .raw() before the query starts (before await, .then(), or .execute()) to ensure binary formats are requested.

```ts
const rows = await sql`SELECT * FROM users`.raw();
console.log(rows); // [[Buffer, Buffer], [Buffer, Buffer], [Buffer, Buffer]]
```

### Example project structure for concurrent and sequential test files

Shows an example directory layout organizing sequential unit tests and concurrent integration test files.

```sh
my-project/
├── bunfig.toml
├── tests/
│   ├── unit/
│   │   ├── math.test.ts          # Sequential
│   │   └── utils.test.ts         # Sequential
│   └── integration/
│       ├── concurrent-api.test.ts     # Concurrent
│       └── concurrent-database.test.ts # Concurrent
```

### Create a Nuxt project with bun create

Initializes a new Nuxt application using the official create-nuxt CLI tool and displays the interactive setup prompts.

```sh
bun create nuxt@latest my-nuxt-app
```

```txt

### Read a resolved promise's value with Bun.peek()

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/utils.mdx

Use Bun.peek() to read a promise's result without await or .then, but only if the promise has already fulfilled or rejected. This example shows peeking a resolved promise to get its value.

```typescript
import { peek } from "bun";

const promise = Promise.resolve("hi");

// no await!
const result = peek(promise);
console.log(result); // "hi"
```

--------------------------------

### Install and run global packages using bun i -g

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/install/from-npm-install-to-bun-install.mdx

Installs a package globally to `.bun/install/global/node_modules` inside your home directory and executes its CLI binary directly without the `bun run` prefix.

```sh
# Install a package globally
bun i -g eslint

# Run a globally-installed package without the `bun run` prefix
eslint --init
```

### Example output of bun audit fix

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/audit.mdx

Shows the plan printed by `bun audit fix`, including fixed packages, packages blocked by a dependent's range, and packages with no published fix. The final counts reflect the re-audit after installing.

### Set up Bun development environment with Nix flake

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/project/contributing.mdx

Use the repository's Nix flake to get all dependencies in an isolated, reproducible environment without sudo. After entering the environment, run `bun bd` to build Bun.

```bash
nix develop
bun bd
```

### Build and run the TanStack Start server

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/tanstack-start.mdx

Builds the application and starts the custom server. The server listens on port 3000 by default or uses the PORT environment variable if specified.

```sh
bun run build
bun run start
```

### Initialize project with bun init

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/typescript.mdx

Runs project initialization in a new directory, automatically generating a configured `tsconfig.json` file.

```sh
bun init
```

--------------------------------

### Get, set, delete, and fix package.json fields with bun pm pkg

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/pm.mdx

Examples of each bun pm pkg operation. With --json, a value that is not valid JSON is an error. set, delete, and fix accept --dry-run, which prints the resulting package.json instead of writing it.

```bash
# get
bun pm pkg get name                               # single property
bun pm pkg get name version                       # multiple properties
bun pm pkg get                                    # entire package.json
bun pm pkg get scripts.build                      # nested property

# set
bun pm pkg set name="my-package"                  # simple property
bun pm pkg set scripts.test="jest" version=2.0.0  # multiple properties
bun pm pkg set private=true --json                # JSON values with --json flag
bun pm pkg set 'keywords[]=cli'                   # append to an array (created if missing)
bun pm pkg set 'contributors[0].name=Jane'        # update an array element

# delete
bun pm pkg delete description                     # single property
bun pm pkg delete scripts.test contributors[0]    # multiple/nested

# fix
bun pm pkg fix                                    # auto-fix common issues
```

--------------------------------

### Force refresh cached registry metadata with bun add or bun install

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx

Use --force to fetch fresh metadata before the 5-minute cache expires, for example after publishing a new version. Bun re-asks the registry for every range or tag it must resolve and rewrites the cached manifest.

```bash
bun add <pkg> --force
# or, in a project without a lockfile
bun install --force
```

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/pm.mdx

Shows the default output format: licenses as headings, packages indented with versions, and a summary line with package count and timing.

```

### Bundle with Bun.build API

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/bundler/index.mdx

Use the Bun.build API to bundle the entrypoint file and output to the ./out directory.

```ts
await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ["./index.tsx"],
  outdir: "./out",
});
```

### Install a package with bun install

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/snippets/cli/install.mdx

Basic CLI usage for installing a named package at a specific version. Run from a terminal in your project directory.

```sh
bun install <name>@<version>
```

--------------------------------

### Install and run Bun in a GitHub Actions workflow

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/runtime/cicd.mdx

Use the oven-sh/setup-bun@v2 action to install Bun in a GitHub Actions runner and execute bun or bunx commands.

```yaml
name: my-workflow
jobs:
  my-job:
    name: my-job
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # ...
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2 # [!code ++]

      # run any `bun` or `bunx` command
      - run: bun install # [!code ++]
      - run: bun index.ts # [!code ++]
      - run: bun run build # [!code ++]
```

--------------------------------

### ArrayBufferSink.prototype.start(options?)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/streams.mdx

Configures and starts the sink with buffer allocation and streaming options.

```APIDOC
## start(options?)

### Description
Initializes the internal buffer and streaming settings for the sink.

### Syntax
```ts
sink.start(options?: {
  asUint8Array?: boolean;
  highWaterMark?: number;
  stream?: boolean;
}): void;
```

### Parameters
- **options** (object) - Optional configuration object.
  - **asUint8Array** (boolean) - Optional. If set, output is returned as a `Uint8Array`.
  - **highWaterMark** (number) - Optional. Preallocates an internal buffer of this size to improve performance with small chunk sizes.
  - **stream** (boolean) - Optional. On `flush()`, returns written data as `Uint8Array` / `ArrayBuffer` and restarts writes from the beginning of the buffer.

### Return Value
- `void`
```

### Install a specific version of Bun on Windows

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/util/upgrade.mdx

Installs a specific version of Bun via the PowerShell installation script on Windows.

```powershell
iex "& {$(irm https://bun.sh/install.ps1)} -Version 1.3.3"
```

### Install without creating a lockfile with --no-save

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/lockfile.mdx

Use `bun install --no-save` to install without creating a lockfile.

```bash
bun install --no-save
```

--------------------------------

### Install dependencies for specific packages using --filter

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx

Use the --filter flag to install dependencies for a subset of packages in a monorepo. The first command installs for all workspaces except pkg-c; the second installs only for pkg-a in ./packages/pkg-a.

```bash
# Install dependencies for all workspaces except `pkg-c`
bun install --filter '!pkg-c'

# Install dependencies for only `pkg-a` in `./packages/pkg-a`
bun install --filter './packages/pkg-a'
```

### Parse ordered list start number with leading zeros

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/js/bun/md/spec.txt

Demonstrates that leading zeros in start numbers are parsed to their integer value for the list start attribute.

```markdown
003. ok
.
<ol start="3">
<li>ok</li>
</ol>
```
